text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Arrested paedophiles in Barcelona sold pornographic films for 10 years.
- Conscientous objectors who are not called in time to do civil service are exempt from completing their service.
EL MUNDO
- Barcelona paedophiles abused and used pictures of 40 children.
- Via Digital will broadcast football and will cost 2,500 pesetas a month for 35 channels.
- Basque Nationalist Party leader Xabier Arzalluz again defends dialogue with ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna.
DIARIO 16
- Twelve people arrested with links to network that abused more than 40 children in Barcelona.
ABC
- Social and political sectors call out for modification of penal code and more strict punishments for people involved in child crimes.
CINCO DIAS

- Industry Minister Josep Pique privatises steel and aluminium. A 35 percent stake of steel producer CSI is sold to Luxembourg's Arbed, while aluminium group Inespal is sold to U.S.-based Aluminium Company of America (Alcoa).
- The summer sales arrive on bourse with main companies losing more than 10 percent from their recent highs.
- Santander posts attributable profit of 59.7 billion pesetas in first half.
EXPANSION
- Six biggest Spanish banks end first half with historic net profit of 224.64 billion pesetas.
- Via Digital will broadcast football and premiere films to offset offer by CanalSatelite.
- Alcoa will pay 61.5 billion pesetas for Inespal.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Five biggest Spanish banks have attributable profit of 207.56 billion pesetas in first half of year, a 15.42 percent increase on 1996.
- Democratic Union of Cataluna wants increase in tax deductions for children.
- Bourse falls 1.70 percent and general index stands at 589.81.
